operations.text: 0.3.25 changes what an audit blocks on and what a plan must carry, in five parts. One: review.md gains the section A blocker names a loss, one text for both audits - at plan readiness and at code review a BLOCKER names what is lost if the work runs exactly as written (stored data or money wrong, an access or tenancy hole, a failing or blocking migration, a race that loses a write, something the user sees wrong or cannot do, a decision left to the Writer, a proof that does not test the ticket's own product property), while a finding about wording, order, proof form, evidence or record is a note that opens no revision and no pass; the readiness brief carries the same text, and the readiness triage gains the dispositions note: land and note: drop. Two: a plan no longer restates the project's verification procedure - a ticket names its own tests, resets and acceptance commands and cites the test policy by one line, the planner brief gains the TEST POLICY slot, and readiness classes 8 and 11 and check 5 read only what the plan itself introduces. Three: plan-form duties scale with the change - read / lock / write rows only for a function whose write order, lock or statement set the plan changes, and closing-grep sets only for a symbol whose definition the plan changes. Three more sentences follow the same rule: a readiness proof is a blocker only when it cannot observe the ticket's own property (ticket.md, section Proof-surface feasibility), a finding closed by wording is fixed in a revision only when it names a loss (plan.md), and a ticket cut is a blocker only when a ticket cannot ship alone without a loss (readiness class 16). Four: measurement is two fixed-form rows starting with the cell pnp-measure, one in the plan index at its landing and one in the ticket record at its close, filled from figures the COO already holds, an unknown figure written as - and never asked; the context-size measurements of /pnp:plan and the question to the operator are gone. Five: a PRODUCT STAGE line in the readiness, code-review and planner briefs names the project's product stage - what this stage does not ask for is a note, never a blocker, what it lists as mandatory is not loosened, and it never lowers the floor. This update re-renders review.md, plan.md and ticket.md, each additions block carried, and the Reviewer agent where one was rendered. The overrides seed now carries a section Product stage, but your own overrides document is never rewritten: write that section yourself when you want one - Changed only by the operator. Where the product is: <fill in>. Not asked at this stage - never a blocker, never planned for: <fill in, or none>. Mandatory at this stage - nothing here is loosened: <fill in, or none>. With no such section the PRODUCT STAGE line reads none and the pass is judged without it. A Claude-hosted Reviewer whose .claude/agents/reviewer.md this update did not re-render - an unrecorded file is never overwritten - is re-rendered by a /pnp:roles --set or --reset run.
